newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - March 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - March 7.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Friday:
* Seeking to thwart a hostile takeover by H.F. Ahmanson, Great Western agreed to be acquired by Washington Mutual in a $6.6 billion stock deal that creates the country's largest savings and loan.
* Cheaper retailers such as Dollar General and high-priced retailers such as Neiman Marcus reported the strongest same-store sales for February, while middle-market retailers continued to struggle.

* As barriers between banking, insurance and brokerage businesses crumble, big banks and other financial giants are considering Wall Street acquisitions, while Wall Street firms step up efforts to take cover through potential alliances of their own.
* Omnicom's BBDO Worldwide dropped out of the running for Delta Air Lines estimated $100 million advertising account, accusing its client of 51 years of rigging the review to end their relationship.
* Walt Disney's ABC network named longtime ABC news President Roone Arledge to the new position of ABC News chairman.
* ITT Corp agreed to sell its half interest in Madison Square Garden to its partner, Cablevision Systems Corp, for $650 million.

* Negotiations to settle the Texaco race discrimination suit have collapsed, and former Texaco executive Richard Lundwall may be indicted on charges of destroying documents, people with knowledge of the situation say.
* A government report says orders with American factories rose 2.5 percent in January.
* Texas Instruments said it would shift its focus to specialised chips known as digital signal processors used in cellular telephones, computer modems and automobiles.
* National Semiconductor exceeded analysts' estimates by reporting a gain in revenue and an 86 percent surge in quarterly earnings.
* The Dow industrials ended 1.15 points lower at 6,944.70.
* A Federal Tax Court rejected a method proposed by Merrill Lynch to allow Colgate-Palmolive to avoid taxes on $98 million in gains from the sale of a subsidiary.
* An auction for rights to explore for oil and gas in the Gulf of Mexico drew the highest bids in 12 years.

* A California securities firm, WS Clearing, remained closed Thursday because of lack of capital, sending the penny stocks of some small companies such as Hollywood Productions Metropolitan Health Networks tumbling.
* Advertising by liquor and beer companies and tobacco companies on the World Wide Web is drawing criticism from children's advocates such as the National Parent Teachers Association.
